description: Webhook messages. The spec types every message in a `messages` webhook (`IncomingMessage`, a union of `TextMessage`, `ImageMessage`, `ButtonMessage`, ...) with the shapes used to SEND messages: each requires `messaging_product`, `recipient_type` and `to`, and none has `from`, `id` or `timestamp` (the unified spec merged the send and webhook schemas; same-named schemas such as `TextMessage` kept the send version). Live webhooks on 2026-11-18 (v23.0 app, test number, through a tunnel) carried text, reply (`context: { from, id }`), image (`caption`, `mime_type`, `sha256`, `id`, `url`), voice note (`audio` with `voice: true`), reaction (`message_id`, `emoji`), shared contact (`contacts[]` with `name`, `phones`, `vcard`, `origin`) and location (`latitude`/`longitude` as numbers, `name`, `address`, `url`) messages, each as `{ from, from_user_id, id, timestamp, type, <type>: {...} }`, without `messaging_product`, `recipient_type` or `to`. `IncomingMessage` becomes that one structure with one optional member per type. `video`, `document` and `sticker` share the image/audio media object, as in Meta's webhook reference (https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages); `button`, `interactive`, `order`, `system` and `errors` reuse the spec's own content shapes. System messages use the same structure. Status webhooks from the same runs also carried `statuses[].recipient_user_id`, `statuses[].pricing.type` (`regular`) and a top-level `contacts` list whose items have `wa_id` and `user_id` but no `profile`; message webhooks carried `contacts[].user_id` too. Those are added as optional and `profile` is no longer required. A second run the same day carried a button reply (`interactive: { type: "button_reply", button_reply: { id, title } }`), a list reply (`interactive: { type: "list_reply", list_reply: { id, title, description } }`), a video, a document (`filename`) and a sticker (`animated: false`), all with the same envelope; the interactive reply shapes gain `type` and the media object gains `animated`.
